title: Messengers from John the Baptist and Rest for the Weary

questions.question: When John heard in prison about the deeds of the Christ, he sent his disciples to ask Jesus what question?
options: "Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?"
"When will you overthrow the Romans?"
"Why have you left me here in prison?"
"Are you Elijah who was to return?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?"
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:2-3 (ESV): "Now when John heard in prison about the deeds of the Christ, he sent word by his disciples and said to him, 'Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?'"

questions.question: What evidence did Jesus tell John's disciples to report back to John?
options: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached to them
He had fed thousands with five loaves
He had walked on water
He had cleansed the temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached to them
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:4-5 (ESV): "Go and tell John what you hear and see: the blind receive their sight and the lame walk, lepers are cleansed and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them."

questions.question: Jesus told the crowds that John the Baptist was more than a prophet, because he was the one about whom it was written: "Behold, I send my..." what?
options: Messenger before your face
Servant to pave the way
Angel of the Lord
Elijah in the flesh
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:10 (ESV): "This is he of whom it is written, 'Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.'" (Quoting Malachi 3:1)

questions.question: Jesus said among those born of women there has arisen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet who is greater than he?
options: The one who is least in the kingdom of heaven
The disciples of Christ
The Apostle Paul
King David
questions.correctAnswer: The one who is least in the kingdom of heaven
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:11 (ESV): "Truly, I say to you, among those born of women there has arisen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet the one who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he."

questions.question: From the days of John the Baptist until now, what has the kingdom of heaven suffered?
options: Violence
Persecution
Famine
Deception
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:12 (ESV): "From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven has suffered violence, and the violent take it by force."

questions.question: If people are willing to accept it, who does Jesus say John the Baptist is?
options: He is Elijah who is to come
He is the Messiah ben Joseph
He is Isaiah reborn
He is the last of the Judges
questions.correctAnswer: He is Elijah who is to come
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:14 (ESV): "and if you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah who is to come."

questions.question: How did Jesus describe "this generation" regarding their response to John and Himself?
options: Like children sitting in the marketplaces saying, "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn."
Like sheep wandering without a shepherd
Like a vineyard that produces only wild grapes
Like an army that refuses to fight
questions.correctAnswer: Like children sitting in the marketplaces saying, "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn."
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:16-17 (ESV): "But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling to their playmates, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn.'"

questions.question: John came neither eating nor drinking, and the people said he had a demon. What did they call the Son of Man who came eating and drinking?
options: A glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners
A false prophet and a deceiver
A Roman sympathizer
A zealot wanting to be King
questions.correctAnswer: A glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:18-19 (ESV): "The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look at him! A glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'"

questions.question: Why did Jesus begin to denounce the cities where most of His mighty works had been done?
options: Because they did not repent
Because they did not pay the temple tax
Because they tried to make Him a king
Because they followed John the Baptist instead
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:20 (ESV): "Then he began to denounce the cities where most of his mighty works had been done, because they did not repent."

questions.question: Which cities does Jesus say it will be more bearable for on the day of judgment than for Chorazin and Bethsaida?
options: Tyre and Sidon
Sodom and Gomorrah
Nineveh and Babylon
Jericho and Ai
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:21-22 (ESV): "...if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon... But I tell you, it will be more bearable on the day of judgment for Tyre and Sidon than for you."

questions.question: If the mighty works done in Capernaum had been done in Sodom, what did Jesus say would have happened to Sodom?
options: It would have remained until this day
It would have conquered the surrounding nations
It would have been the holy city instead of Jerusalem
It would have built fifty temples
questions.correctAnswer: It would have remained until this day
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:23 (ESV): "And you, Capernaum... if the mighty works done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day."

questions.question: At that time Jesus declared, "I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to..." whom?
options: Little children
The poor and destitute
The priests in the temple
The righteous seeking truth

questions.question: According to Jesus, who is the only one who truly knows the Father?
options: The Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him
Those who keep the Law of Moses perfectly
The angels standing before His throne
Every man, woman, and child intuitively
questions.correctAnswer: The Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:27 (ESV): "No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him."

questions.question: What simple invitation does Jesus give to "all who labor and are heavy laden"?
options: "Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."
"Lay your burdens down at the altar in Jerusalem."
"Pray for strength individually."
"Flee into the wilderness."
questions.correctAnswer: "Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:28 (ESV): "Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."

questions.question: Jesus tells us to take His yoke upon us and learn from Him, because He is gentle and lowly in heart. What does He say about His yoke and burden?
options: "For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."
"For my yoke requires great strength to bear."
"For my yoke is the Law, and my burden is truth."
"For my yoke breaks the back of the wicked."
questions.correctAnswer: "For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:30 (ESV): "For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."

key_verse_text: "Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."
